items.summaryJa: Google Cloudの新製品 Gemini for healthcare は、断片化した医療データを統合して多段階のワークフローを人間の監督下で完了させる、安全で統治されたオーケストレーション層を提供します。医療機関向けには、医療記録の統合・事前準備・保険適用の審査などの作業を支援する「スキル」と、臨床・財務・運用システムに直接接続するコネクター、オープンなエコシステム、ポリシー統制機能の4つの構成要素が用意されています。HIPAA準拠を前提とし、EHRや請求システムと安全に連携しつつ、モデルの選択肢を維持できる点が特徴です。

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
items.summary: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare to unify clinical data and automate workflows. Reduce administrative burnout. See how it works.
items.titleJa: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.

本動画は、Qiita記事「大学の運営費削減と任期付きポジションが需要を冷やすメカニズム」を対話形式で深掘りしたもので、基盤費を削って競争的資金に依存させる政策が、長期的には研究力とマクロ経済需要を悪化させるという結論を数学的に示しています。マクロ経済的には、安定した雇用・研究環境を「エンジン」として整備することが不可欠だと主張し、教育・科学技術・人的資本の重要性を位置づけています。

items.title: Decision models take 26% of requests; Anthropic now wins new teams 2:1
items.summary: AI Gateway Production Index — November 2026 Every month, AI Gateway routes more than 100 trillion tokens between production applications and AI labs. That traffic gives us a view of what AI usage looks like in today’s enterprise and startup landscape across language, decision, voice, image, and video models. We publish it here monthly. See the Production Index reports from August , September , and October . November 2026 Summary In six weeks, decision models grew to one in four gateway requests, while accounting for half a cent of every dollar spent. Close to a third of all paid teams used one in October. Among teams processing over 10 billion tokens a month, seven in ten used a decision model. About 11% of paid teams used a voice model in October, up from 4% in July. OpenAI and Anthropic now reach about the same share of paid teams, and new teams in October picked Anthropic nearly two to one . OpenAI’s share of gateway spend, meanwhile, is up by two-thirds since December. More than half of language-model requests went to models less than two months old, up from less than three in ten. Within one month of a typical model’s peak usage, three in four of the teams using it have moved on. Decision models account for 26% of all requests Production AI is splitting into two jobs: generation and judgment. Until recently, when software needed to make a quick call, a team could use either a fixed rule that was cheap but rigid, or a language model that was smart but slow and expensive. Decision models are now a third option. They classify, score, or pick between choices instead of generating text, and cost about a seventieth as much per request as a language model. They arrived on AI Gateway in mid-September, and there are now 15 decision models available from eight different vendors. In October, nearly a third of paid teams on AI Gateway used a decision model. About 11% of paid teams used a decision model without sending a single request to a text-generating model. Decision models cost far less per token and give very short answers, so even though they received about one in four gateway requests in October, they accounted for just 0.53% of total spend. Almost all of that request volume went to Jev from TypeSafe AI, which alone received nearly four times Anthropic’s total requests. For every $1 teams spent on Jev, they spent $64 on Anthropic models. Decision models are most common among the teams that run the most AI. Just over one in five teams running fewer than 10 million tokens used a decision model in October. At 100 million to 1 billion tokens, nearly half used one. Above 10 billion, seven in ten did. This is partly because big teams use more of everything. The top 1% of teams by spend use a median of 29 different models, and the bottom tenth use only one. It’s also volume. The more requests a team sends, the more it has to gain from a model that makes simple decisions faster and far more cost-effectively. Voice adoption is up 2.6x since July About one in nine paid teams used a voice model in October, up from one in 24 in July, an increase of 161%. New teams are using voice, and existing teams are adding it. Among teams that paid in both July and October, the share using voice went from 5% to 14%. Teams that use voice are also using more of it. The share of teams sending at least 100 voice requests a month grew fivefold, and six in ten of September’s voice teams returned in October, up from fewer than half in July. A spoken conversation with an AI app takes three steps: A voice model turns the user’s speech into text A language model writes the reply Another voice model reads the reply back to the user Most voice teams use just one or two of these pieces. Use of speech-to-text models has nearly tripled since July, and text-to-speech has more than tripled. Some models do all three steps on their own. In July, about a quarter of voice teams used one of these all-in-one models, and one in six assembled the pieces themselves. By October, those numbers had swapped. For most teams, voice is a new way for users to talk to an app or agent they already have. Teams’ preferred language models stay in the middle, and they can add voice at one end or both. Anthropic wins new teams two to one, and OpenAI’s share of spend is up two-thirds Last December, 70 of every 100 paid teams on AI Gateway used an OpenAI model and 48 used an Anthropic model. By October, the two labs were nearly level, with OpenAI at 55 and Anthropic at 54. Both labs now reach more of the teams that have been on the gateway since December, but Anthropic’s reach grew more. The share of these teams using Anthropic rose from about half to two-thirds, while OpenAI’s rose from about three in four to four in five. Most of Anthropic’s gain came from new teams. In October, it was the first-choice lab for nearly twice as many of them as OpenAI. But among the biggest teams, both labs already have nearly everyone. More than nine in ten of the top 1% by spend use both Anthropic and OpenAI. With these teams, the labs now compete for how much of the work each one gets. On that measure, Anthropic still leads, but OpenAI has gained ground. OpenAI now takes nearly 15 cents of every dollar spent on the gateway, up from about 9 in December, while Anthropic’s halved to about 32 cents over the same period. Most AI traffic now runs on models less than two months old Teams are moving to new models almost as fast as labs release them. More than half of October’s language-model requests went to models less than 60 days old. Before September, that share had never passed three in ten. Within each model family, a new version arrives every 61 days at the median, and a typical model peaks within a month of launch. Four weeks later, three in four of the teams using it at its peak aren’t using it anymore, whether or not a successor has shipped in the family. Most of those teams are still on AI Gateway, using other models. Teams switch models frequently, usually to something newer, and often to another lab. In October, about half of teams running at least 10 million tokens a month changed their most-used model. Four in five of those moved to a more recent release, and six in ten moved to a different lab. Older models stay in use, often alongside a newer primary model. Seven in ten teams running at least 10 million tokens a month still used a model at least ten months old in October, but for the typical team it ran less than 3% of its tokens. AI models now have a half-life of about six weeks. That means that, to the teams using them, labs are only as good as their latest model and have to re-earn their business with every new one. Also in October’s data Opus 5.5 was the top model by spend in its first full month. It took about one in seven dollars across all teams. Four of the six most widely used models on AI Gateway are Anthropic’s: Sonnet 5.5 (reaching 26% of paid teams), Haiku 5.5 (22%), Haiku 4.5 (20%), and Opus 5.5 (18%). Jev (28%) and GPT-6 Luna (19%) are the other two. Image and video both had their biggest month yet on AI Gateway. More teams than ever are putting spend on them, and the largest teams are adopting them the fastest. About a third of the top 1% of teams by spend now use an image model, up from a quarter in July. One in six use a video model, up from one in ten. OpenAI’s newest image model, GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, took the lead in image spend in its first full month, followed by its Flare and GPT-Image-2 models. ByteDance’s Seedance 2.5 led video spend for a third month running, ahead of Google’s Veo 3.1 and Kuaishou’s Kling 3.0. About this data This report uses anonymized, aggregate traffic routed through Vercel AI Gateway through October 2026. A few notes on measurement: Spend is estimated at published list prices; actual bills may differ. Paid teams are teams with at least one paid request in the month. Team size is measured by a team’s total tokens that month. Decision models are the models classified as decision models in the AI Gateway model list. Each model version is counted separately. A model’s age is measured from that version’s first day on AI Gateway, and gateway history begins October 20, 2025. Switching rates compare paid teams with at least 10 million tokens in both September and October. A team’s most-used model is measured by tokens. Voice figures begin June 22, 2026. Teams that “assembled the pieces” used speech-to-text, a language model, and text-to-speech on the same day. A new team’s first-choice lab is the lab it sent the most language-model requests to in its first month. All figures use the most recent data and protocol available; prior months may be revised as methodology is updated. Read more about our methodology , and explore or download the public data . items.title: Ampersand from Humans& now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Ampersand from Humans& is now available on AI Gateway for free through November 13, 2026. Ampersand is a model for group conversations. Humans& built Ampersand on Z.ai 's open-weight GLM 5.3 and trained it with reinforcement learning in simulated group conversations that run for up to months of simulated time. Most chat models are built for one person asking a question and the model answering it. Ampersand is trained to take part in a conversation between several people. It reads every message, including the ones not addressed to it, and after each one it decides whether to reply or stay quiet. It is designed to understand individual and shared goals, help people work through disagreements, and recognize when a contribution would be useful. That can mean asking a clarifying question, sharing relevant context, or waiting while people respond to one another. For example: Sam: Heads up, I'm out Friday, driving to my sister's. Alex: Have a good trip! Maya: Let's do the launch rehearsal Friday at 10 with all three of us. Ampersand: Quick flag, Maya: Sam said he's out Friday driving to his sister's, so a Friday 10am rehearsal with all three probably won't work. Might be worth picking a different time so everyone can make it. Your application exposes these actions as caller-defined function tools . send_message delivers a contribution, while pass leaves the conversation quiet until the next human message. Your application executes both tools and records their results. Call it through the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API , or a coding agent. Use humansand/ampersand-v0.1 as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select humansand/ampersand-v0.1 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Ampersand in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

items.titleJa: Taming Typography: Building a Modern CSS Reset
items.summaryJa: 本文では、現代的なCSSリセットを作ることで、タイポグラフィの微調整をリセット範囲内に取り込み、可変フォントやコンテナクエリ、ハイフネーション、行間調整などを組み合わせて安定した文字組みを実現する方法が紹介されています。具体例として、フォントのレンダリングやフォントサイズ調整、 fluid typography、テキストの縦揺れ防止、行頭末の均衡、hyphenationの細かな設定、ダークモード時の視認性補正、モノスペースとサイズ調整の併用などが挙げられ、段落や見出し、引用などの要素ごとに適用する設定が説明されています。最後に、これらの機能は実験的な点やブラウザ差があるため、 guardrails を設けて全体をまとめた tidy-typography.css の提案と、個別の解決策としてのコード解説が位置づけられています。
